text:
maria: quick heads-up — canary telemetry after the kernel-selector tweak shows a noticeable host-side CPU bump in preparse/tokenization. baseline -> canary: +18% CPU across host-preproc pods. link: https://perf/reports/3612347890

kevin: ugh. saw the alert. flamegraph looks dominated by `proto::unpack` and `stream_framer::emit_small_write`. small-write syscalls jump way up. snippet from perf: 
```
proto::unpack 35%
stream_framer::emit_small_write 22%
tokenize::utf8_scan 12%
kv_cache::evict 9%
```

kevin: also tcp retrans stats higher on the canary — suggests lots of Nagle/uncoalesced writes at http/gRPC layer.

maria: good catch. curious if kernel selection change (eager small-batch path for short sequences) increased frequency of tiny frames. that would both increase syscall churn and reduce KV hit locality.

taylor: checked kv metrics — global kv hit-rate fell from 95.8% -> 87.2% during the window. eviction rate doubled. likely more unique prefixes hitting backend, KV cold starts.

sam: reminder: the selector change introduced a preference for the `minibatch_fastpath` kernel when estimated seq_len <= 32 and concurrency < 8. that reduces GPU latency but may fragment host batching and shorten KV cache lifetimes.

maria: hypothesis: selector -> more small, faster kernel runs -> host emits more frequent, smaller network writes -> http2/gRPC frames not coalesced -> increased syscalls + lower KV residency -> CPU regression.

kevin: quick experiment idea: enable host-side coalescing (writev window = 8ms) and bump the `kv_cache_ttl_ms` by 200ms in canary to see effect. cheap rollback if noisy.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: kernel-selector:v2 applied to fleet (id: canary-2026-03-20T11:00Z).

maria: plan: 1) rollback selector change in canary for 2h to verify revert restores baseline. 2) run targeted microbench: 5k requests synthetic (mix short/med sequences) with and without writev coalesce enabled. 3) collect eBPF syscall counters + pprof CPU + kv hit heatmap.

taylor: I already kicked off the microbench harness with coalesce enabled on a subset. initial 10m run: CPU delta down to +3% and kv hit-rate back up to 94.1%. promising.

sam: can you paste the harness command?

taylor: sure —
```bash
./bench-run --rps 500 --mix short:0.6,medium:0.4 --duration 600 \
  --canary-tag kernel-selector=v2 --host-opts coalesce_write_ms=8 --output bench/3612347890-coalesce.json
```

kevin: nice. add `--collect-pprof=1` and `--ebpf-syscall` flags for the next run. we want raw counts for `write` vs `writev` and `sendmsg`.

maria: decision: abort full rollout for now. rollback scheduled and will re-evaluate after microbench + pprof. action owners: maria -> rollback + verify, taylor -> add pprof/ebpf and run bench, kevin -> prepare dashboard tiles (flame + kv heatmap), sam -> propose long-term selector tweak (prefer batching affinity over absolute minimal latency)

kevin: also adding a quick mitigation: opportunistic pretokenize on the ingress proxy for requests under 128 bytes. that should reduce proto::unpack time and unify prefixes hitting kv. prototype patch ready, will canary behind flag.

maria: perfect. please post results here. I'll open a short postmortem if the revert proves causal. thanks folks :thumbsup:

sam: pinging infra team to see if we can tune kernel-selector config remotely without rebuild — that would let us experiment faster.

deploy-bot: canary-rollback: kernel-selector:v2 -> kernel-selector:v1 (initiated by maria)

maria: rollback complete. initial sanity checks: CPU back to +1% vs baseline, kv hit-rate 95.5%. will let this stabilize and then run the full microbench profile.
